card: Introduces `--enable-multiprocess` support to split Bitcoin Core into separate `bitcoin-node`, `bitcoin-wallet`, and `bitcoin-gui` processes communicating over IPC socketpairs via Cap'n Proto. Today, all components share a single monolithic process, meaning bugs or vulnerabilities in the GUI or wallet can compromise the validating node. This PR is a centerpiece of the process separation project (#28722) to isolate components and enable OS sandboxing. It depends on #29409 and enables socket connection options in #19460 and #19461.
evidence: Part of the multi-year process separation architectural project (#28722) to enforce privilege boundaries and sandboxing across node components.

Author description: 'This PR adds an --enable-multiprocess configure option which builds new bitcoin-node, bitcoin-wallet, and bitcoin-gui executables with relevant functionality isolated into different processes.'
problem: Bitcoin Core's node, wallet, and GUI run within a single monolithic address space, which blurs privilege boundaries and means a security vulnerability, crash, or memory corruption in GUI or wallet code can compromise the entire node and consensus validation.
scope_notes: Very large change spanning 136 files. Contains an embedded subtree update of `src/ipc/libmultiprocess`, several large Cap'n Proto interface definition files (`.capnp`) and serialization wrappers, and cross-subsystem changes to process initialization and `btcsignals` callback lifetime.
summary: Adds `--enable-multiprocess` build support allowing Bitcoin Core to run with node, wallet, and GUI functionality separated into isolated processes. Implements Cap'n Proto IPC wrappers for the Node and Wallet interfaces, wires `bitcoin-gui` to spawn a `bitcoin-node` subprocess, and wires `bitcoin-node` to spawn a `bitcoin-wallet` subprocess communicating over socketpairs. Also updates the `libmultiprocess` subtree, improves signal destruction timing in `btcsignals`, and adapts logging and test frameworks for multiprocess execution.
